correctness.rationale: Equations (4.3) and (4.4) are two exact evaluations of the same Volterra identity. Their subtraction necessarily produces a minus sign before the earlier-time integral, whereas the source prints a plus sign. For constant forcing the exact integrals are elementary, yielding the explicit difference-versus-sum formulas. Summing the printed increments at fixed terminal time gives a power sum whose leading term is proportional to 1/Delta, proving inconsistency for every 0<h<=1. The embedded verifier independently checks representative cases and the integer-order exact witness.

value.rationale: The numerical method is used to visualize the article's central claims about fractional order and delay. The defect occurs before numerical approximation: an exact subtraction is printed with the wrong sign. The resulting parent recurrence fails the most basic constant-forcing consistency test and diverges under refinement, so identifying the error materially changes what the published numerical derivation can support. The claim is bounded so that unavailable simulation code is not over-interpreted.
